body: Distributed LLM-agent teams can read the latest shared facts and still act on an obsolete plan. A planner may derive an action from requirement r_3, another agent may commit r_4, and an executor may receive r_4 without replacing the plan derived from r_3. We call this stale-plan execution: state freshness does not establish that the plan authorizing an action remains valid. We introduce PlanFence, a dependency-scoped action-validation protocol. Plans cite the exact public records they used, and an executor validates only the records that can affect the pending external action, replanning once or blocking when validation is incomplete. In 30 controlled live workflows with a post-plan revision, a freshness-only executor acts on the obsolete plan in every task, whereas PlanFence completes all tasks without an invalid action. Controlled replay reveals two conditional boundaries: proactive synchronization yields lower coordination stall at low churn, while PlanFence avoids repeated update-path coordination as churn grows and avoids validating unrelated state as the shared keyspace grows. These are controlled safety and systems-cost results, not general task-accuracy gains.
summaryZh: 新鲜的内存，过时的计划：分布式 LLM 代理内存的依赖范围验证。分布式 LLM 代理团队可以读取最新的共享事实，但仍然按照过时的计划采取行动。规划器可以从需求 r_3 导出操作，另一个代理可以提交 r_4，并且执行器可以接收 r_4，而不替换从 r_3 导出的计划。
